<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="79.176.221.29" /></noinclude><section begin="par119" />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=9}}; even before the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=2}}.—To the same class belongs also the ''Lamedh inscriptionis'' (untranslatable in English, and hardly more than a mere quotation-mark) which introduces the exact wording of an inscription or title; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=1}} ''write upon it''... (the words) {{GHGheb|text=מַהֵר שָׁלָל וגו׳}} (cf. verse 3, where the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} naturally is not used); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|v}}
(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}, originally (according to {{GHGpar|101|a}}) ''separation'',<ref>Cf. O. Molin, ''Om prepositionen'' min ''i Bibelhebreisken'', Upsala, 1893, and especially N. Zerweck, ''Die hebr. Praep.'' min, Leipzig, 1893, who, instead of the partitive meaning (formerly accepted by us also), more correctly takes ‘separation’ as the starting-point of its various uses.</ref> represents both the idea of ''distance, separation'' or ''remoteness from'' something, and that of ''motion away from'' something, hence also ''descent, origin from'' a place, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|w}}
(1) From the idea of ''separation'' is naturally derived on the one hand the sense of (''taken'') ''from among''..., ''e numero'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=1}} ''subtil as none other of the beasts'', &c.; cf. 3:14, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=24}} (so especially after the idea of choosing ''out of''<ref>All the ''partitive'' uses of {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} also come most naturally under this idea of separation ''out of'' a larger class. Thus {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} is used in the sense of ''some, something'', and even ''one'', in such expressions as ''and he slew... also'' {{GHGheb|text=מִשָּׂרֵי יִשְּׂרָאֵל}} (''divers'') ''of the princes of Israel'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=21|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִכָּל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=2}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִדַּם הַפָּר|translate=some of the blood of the bullock}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=12}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=6}} ''my heart doth not reproach me'' {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּמַי|translate=for any}}, i.e. for one, ''of my days''; 38:12 {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּמֶ֫יךָ|translate=one of thy days}}, i.e. ''ever in thy life'' (this explanation is confirmed by {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=6}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=45}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=28|hidebook=1}}). In this way also, the frequently misunderstood Hebrew (and Arabic) idiom is to be explained, by which {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} before {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַחַת}} is equivalent to ''ullus''; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=2}} ''and shall do'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאַחַת מֵהֵ֫נָּה|translate=any one of these things}}; 5:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=10}}; so before a ''nomen unitatis'' (see {{GHGpar|122|t}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=45}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=52}}) {{GHGheb|text=מִשַּֽׂעֲרַת רֹאשׁוֹ|translate=not one hair of his head}}.—{{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} is used in the sense of the Arabic ''min el-beyān'' or explicative ''min'' (often to be simply translated by ''namely''), e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=22}} ''of all that was'', i.e. ''so far as it was'', probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=2}} (=''whomsoever they chose'').</ref> a larger class, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=28}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=5}}, &c.), and on the other hand, the sense of ''without'' (separated, free from...), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=מִקֶּ֫שֶׁת אֻסָּ֫רוּ|translate=without the bow}} (i.e. without one needing to bend a bow against them) ''they were made prisoners''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=45}} {{GHGheb|text=מִכֹּחַ|translate=without strength}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=6}}, as the first half-verse shows, not ''more than burnt offerings'' (as R.V.), but ''and not burnt offerings''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=52|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=24}} ''far from the eyes'', i.e. unobserved by the congregation; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|x}}
Here also belongs the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} after the ideas of ''restraining, withholding from, refusing to'' any one, frequently in pregnant expressions, which we can render only by complete final or consecutive clauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=23}} ''he hath rejected thee'' {{GHGheb|text=מִמֶּ֫לֶךְ|translate=away from}} (being) ''king'', instead of {{GHGheb|text=מִֽהְיוֹת מ׳}} (as in verse 26), ''that thou be no longer king''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵעִיר|translate=so that it is no longer a city}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=11}} ''he bindeth the streams'' {{GHGheb|text=מִבְּכִי|translate=that they trickle not}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=6|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מִקְּבֹר|translate=that thou shouldst not bury thy dead}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|y}}
The {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} has a still more pregnant force in those examples in which the idea of precluding from anything is only indirectly contained in the preceding verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=1}} ''his eyes were dim'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽרְאֹה|translate=away from seeing}}, i.e. ''so that he could not see''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=8}} ''Ephraim shall be broken in pieces'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵעָם|translate=that it be not a people}} (just as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=2}}, 42, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=5}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=2|verse=62}} (for other pregnant constructions with {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} see below, ff)<ref>On the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} to express the comparative, which likewise depends on the idea of ''distance from...'', cf. below, {{GHGpar|133|a}}; on {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} as expressing the distance of time from a fixed limit, in the sense of ''after'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵהָקִיץ|translate=after awaking}} (cf. ἐξ, ἀρίστου, ''ab itinere''), or ''after the lapse of...'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=2}}, and very frequently {{GHGheb|text=מִקֵּץ|translate=from the end of}}, i.e. ''after the lapse of...'', see the Lexicon; also for the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} to represent ''resting beside'' anything, like the Latin ''prope abesse ab''...</ref>; on {{GHGheb|text=מִבְּלִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵין|translate=without}}, cf. {{GHGpar|152|y}}.<section end="par119" /><noinclude>
